facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He feels like he is running on fumes.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work situation caused burnout
facts.content: Daniel lost a big client, and half of his team moved onto a rescue plan. He ended up doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, half of the team got moved onto the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Work thoughts continue at night
facts.content: Daniel thinks about work even when he is not working. He is at his desk by 7 and still answering messages at 10 that night.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 that night. Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Sleep quality is terrible
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible, and he sleeps about 4 hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours.

facts.heading: Wakes up at 3 AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at 3 in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Head pain upon waking
facts.content: Daniel's head hurts when he wakes up at 3 AM.
facts.evidence: My head just hurts.

facts.heading: Worry about work schedule
facts.content: Daniel worries about shipping schedules, the client, and whether he has forgotten something when he wakes up.
facts.evidence: Shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something.

facts.heading: Delaying sleep until 5 AM
facts.content: Daniel lies until about 5 and then gets up to make tea.
facts.evidence: Then I lie until about 5 and get up and make tea.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's symptoms
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, he's slower, he gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Father is the strong one
facts.content: Daniel's father is always being the strong one and having a dream.
facts.evidence: He's having a dream and he's always being the strong one.

facts.heading: Drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel is the one who drives his father to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks, it's about an hour each way.

facts.heading: Sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's angry sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My angry sister Hannah lives in Toronto.

facts.heading: Daniel feels responsible for care
facts.content: All the care for their father falls on Daniel.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls of me.

facts.heading: Guilt about expressing feelings
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying anything because his father feels selfish to be tired when he is ill.
facts.evidence: He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill. So I don't say anything to anyone.

facts.heading: Sister calls father weekly
facts.content: Hannah calls their father every Sunday.
facts.evidence: She calls him every Sunday.

facts.heading: Daniel is not fine
facts.content: Daniel tells Hannah he is not fine.
facts.evidence: That I'm not fine.

facts.heading: Daniel's desire for sister to know
facts.content: Daniel wants his sister to know that he is not fine and that he sits in a hospital car park.
facts.evidence: That I'm not fine. That some days I sit in a car park at a hospital for 10 minutes before

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests that were all normal. The GP said it was stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She had blood tests. They were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion.

facts.heading: GP advised no talk therapy
facts.content: The GP said Daniel had not got the time to talk to someone.
facts.evidence: She said I hadn't got the time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked time
facts.content: Claire booked time with Daniel to stop him from disappearing.
facts.evidence: A girlfriend booked her, to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is patient and makes tea for Daniel. She does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire is worried
facts.content: Daniel sees that Claire is worrying about herself too.
facts.evidence: But I can see she's worrying about her too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped weekend plans
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel if he wanted to go away for the weekend.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails cause stress
facts.content: Daniel feels worst about not saying yes to plans because of emails. He has to respond to 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel questions if rest has a price because he cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price? Yeah, exactly.

facts.heading: Ran three years weekly
facts.content: Daniel ran every Saturday morning for three years and has done it for six years.
facts.evidence: I'm going to be three years every Saturday morning. I've done it for six years.

facts.heading: Stopped running recently
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago.

facts.heading: Legs feel like lead
facts.content: Daniel's legs feel like lead after stopping running.
facts.evidence: My legs feel like lead.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself.

facts.heading: Running was escape
facts.content: Running was the one time in the week nobody could reach Daniel.
facts.evidence: It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Peterson sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: He sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answering emails is fear
facts.content: Daniel answers every email even if he is not bad because Claire hates it.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm not bad. Claire hates it.

facts.heading: Fear of not answering
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that his boss will think he is not committed if he does not answer.
facts.evidence: Dan, he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid of being let go due to a restructuring this spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Fear of relief feeling
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that if he is let go, his boss will think he would be relieved.
facts.evidence: He'd think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Tiredness and irritability
facts.content: Daniel moves apart from tiredness and is irritable.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Heart racing during rest
facts.content: Daniel slept at a colleague or nothing and sat in the toilets for ten minutes. His heart was going and his hands were shaking.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Heart attack experience
facts.content: Daniel experienced a heart attack that passed. This has happened a couple of times before.
facts.evidence: I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed. Has it happened before? A couple of times.

facts.heading: Heart attack location
facts.content: Daniel experienced a heart attack on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that he is losing it or going to end up coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up, like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Evening wine consumption
facts.content: Daniel has started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off.

facts.heading: Wine consumption frequency
facts.content: Daniel drinks two or three glasses of wine in the evenings.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Feeling about wine
facts.content: Daniel feels easy about the wine and states it works for an hour.
facts.evidence: Easy. It works for an hour.

facts.heading: Waking time
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning.
facts.evidence: I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Feeling about coping
facts.content: Daniel feels that listing things wrong feels like he is holding a great deal on his own.
facts.evidence: It feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me. I hear a person who has been holding a great deal on his own for a long time.

facts.heading: Relief from speaking out
facts.content: Daniel felt a bit of relief after saying what he was carrying.
facts.evidence: Strange. A bit of relief actually. Like putting it on bad, but I didn't realize I was carrying.

facts.heading: What Daniel carries
facts.content: Daniel thinks the nights are what he wants to put down first.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Grandfather's behavior
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather never complained about anything at work.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything. Not once.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being there.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: What Daniel says to self
facts.content: Daniel wants to tell his grandfather he is not weak but very tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. Just very tired.

facts.heading: Belief about self-worth
facts.content: Daniel is unsure if he believes he is not weak yet.
facts.evidence: Maybe. I don't know if I believe it yet.

facts.heading: Proposed coping strategy
facts.content: Daniel is willing to try a very small change to his routine.
facts.evidence: Would you be willing to try something small? Depends how small.

facts.heading: Proposed time for phone off
facts.content: Daniel suggested a fixed time to switch off his phone.
facts.evidence: A fixed time in the evening when you switch off your phone, even for 20 minutes.

facts.heading: Proposed time for phone off
facts.content: Daniel suggested half past nine as a possible time to try the change.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine perhaps.

facts.content: Daniel felt tired but lighter after the session.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.

facts.heading: Acknowledged difficulty speaking

facts.evidence: Very normal. It takes energy to say it loud loud.
